title: SLA-aware fleet partitioning and proportional autoscaler
author: Asha Patel
description: Introduce SLA-aware fleet partitioning and a proportional autoscaler that allocates reserved capacity to tenant partitions based on SLO priorities and recent utilization. This change creates a new Partition Allocator that groups capacity into small SLO domains (e.g., low-latency, standard, best-effort), extends reservation accounting with per-partition watermarks and decay logic, and plugs a proportional autoscaler which uses soft thresholds and credit buckets to drive scale-out/scale-in decisions. Motivation: customers running Dedicated pools require predictable throughput guarantees for different SLAs while still allowing safe bursting and cluster-level utilization efficiency. Key design points: 1) Partitioning is configurable via operator CRD; partitions map to tenant tags and can be hot-swapped. 2) Reservation watermarks and decay protect against noisy spikes by smoothing effective reserved capacity over a sliding window with exponential decay coefficient. 3) Proportional autoscaler computes target instances per partition as baseline_reserved + alpha * utilization_delta, bounded by min/max allocation and respecting cluster headroom. 4) Burst pacing: tenants above their partition share are served from temporary burst credits which decrement and are replenished on cooled down utilization patterns. 5) Backpressure and graceful fallback: when cluster headroom exhausted we apply model-fallback routing and elastic throttling instead of hard denial. 6) Telemetry: new metrics partition/p95_latency, partition/burst_credit, partition/allocated_instances, and partition/reservation_watermark; added histogram bucketting for per-partition utilization for percentile reporting. Compatibility & migration: partitions default to a single legacy partition to maintain existing behavior; migration opt-in via feature flag cluster.enablePartitioning; rolling upgrade tolerated by version gates. Safety: scale decisions are rate-limited with 60s cooldown per partition; preemption is disabled by default and gated behind operator policy. Testing & rollout: unit tests, integration harness simulating multi-tenant noisy neighbors, and a canary rollout plan with gradual partition splits at 10/30/60/100% traffic. CI: unit + integration + perf; manual canary on staging. Release-note: adds SLA-aware partitioning and proportional autoscaler to Dedicated fleets; operators must opt-in to enable partitioning. Referenced Linear: ENG-2141, SRE-732.

review_comments: Daniel Kim: Overall nice design. A couple of questions: how do we reason about large tenants that span partitions? Is cross-partition burst transfer allowed?

Asha Patel: Answered - tenants are assigned to a single partition via tag; cross-partition transfer is not automatic to avoid SLA violations; operator can re-tag tenant to migrate it. Updated docs with migration section.
Sofia Martinez: Please ensure we've got observability hooks for per-partition headroom so SRE can set alerts; also add an event when a partition hits burst credit exhaustion.
Asha Patel: Added partition/burst_credit and partition/allocated_instances metrics and emitted k8s events on exhaustion. Also added alert examples to docs.
Liam O'Connor: Unit tests look good. Integration harness reproduced regression scenario; suggested lowering alpha in the proportional formula to reduce oscillation.
Asha Patel: Tuned alpha from 0.4 to 0.25 and added a hysteresis window to reduce flip-flopping. Added stress tests in integration suite.
SRE: Approved after staging canary OK.
Release manager: Verified rollout playbook and upgrade compatibility. Approved to merge.
release_notes: Adds optional SLA-aware fleet partitioning and a proportional autoscaler for Dedicated pools. Operators must enable cluster.enablePartitioning to opt in. New telemetry: partition/p95_latency, partition/burst_credit, partition/allocated_instances, partition/reservation_watermark. See docs/ops/partitioning-and-slos.md for migration and rollout guidance.
